data.name: Close Your Eyes [Old Version]
data.detailed_description:
This is the older version, the game has been Remade:

Close Your Eyes has been remade, deeply reimagined, and released as a commercial product with lots of new content onto Steam, simply as "Close Your Eyes". The original freeware version will stay here on Steam for people to download and play freely, but the remake will be getting all future support and I hope to make a surprising and personal horror experience.


Acerca do jogo

Welcome, Ladies & Gentlemen!



A-ha, how y'all doing? Now, the name of the game is to answer truest to yourself. There's no right and wrong, everyone's a winner! Ooorrr a loser, depending how you think about it. Life is all about perception, you see. Onto the first question!

You're a murderer, we all know it. But do you think you are?



Through a stroke of sheer luck, you've managed to escape death row. Taking to an underground subway, you must try to find your salvation. Can you break free of the past that binds you? And please, can you close your eyes? Just close them.

  • Originally started as a 2014 Ludum Dare created RPG Maker Horror Game, reworked twice to become a brand new terrifying experience.
  • Enter a horrific & twisted surreal world full of diabolical traps, puzzles, & questionnaires.
  • Featuring original voice-work, artwork, & music to help create an unsettling atmosphere.
  • Multiple endings and a variety of secrets encourage multiple playthroughs, as things are not always what they seem.

data.short_description: A redux version of a 2014 Ludum Dare RPG Maker Horror Game. A poor little marshmallow escapes death row into an underground subway system, where they're asked questions by a mysterious game show host. Updated in 2025 with new content.

content_descriptors.notes: Close Your Eyes stars a murderer who's escaped execution at death row for hanging. During the course of the game, we explore their complicated history and current mental state in these affairs. The game has another character who writes very explicit notes to the main character, depicting unwanted creepy sexually charged comments and written depictions of violence. Gore is not very frequent in the game, but there is a couple scenes of sudden drawn gore meant to be a bit shocking in a couple of the game's 8 endings.

reviews.review:
Close Your Eyes [Old Version] is an intriguing psychological horror adventure that proves an unsettling atmosphere and imaginative storytelling can be more effective than elaborate graphics or complicated gameplay systems. Developed and published by Yai Gameworks, this free-to-play indie experience combines surreal exploration, disturbing psychological themes, environmental puzzles, and mysterious encounters into an unpredictable journey. Its greatest strength lies in its ability to transform seemingly innocent imagery into something deeply uncomfortable, creating a distinctive horror experience that rewards curiosity, patience, and interpretation.

The story follows a peculiar marshmallow-like protagonist who escapes execution after being convicted of murder. Seeking freedom from a troubled past, the character enters an underground subway system that gradually becomes a gateway into an increasingly bizarre and threatening world. Rather than presenting a straightforward escape narrative, the game explores guilt, identity, personal responsibility, and the uncertainty surrounding one's own memories. A mysterious game show host further complicates the journey by asking uncomfortable questions that challenge the protagonist's understanding of morality and reality. This unusual narrative framework establishes an atmosphere where answers remain elusive and appearances cannot always be trusted.

Gameplay primarily revolves around exploration, environmental interaction, puzzle-solving, and uncovering narrative secrets. Players navigate strange locations filled with disturbing imagery, hidden passages, unusual obstacles, and potentially dangerous traps. Questionnaires introduce another interesting dimension by encouraging players to consider their responses rather than simply selecting obvious solutions. Although the mechanics are relatively straightforward, the unpredictable environments maintain a persistent feeling of vulnerability. The absence of elaborate combat systems allows the experience to concentrate on psychological tension and discovery, making it particularly appealing to enthusiasts of narrative-driven horror.

The atmosphere is undoubtedly one of the game's most impressive accomplishments. Its pixel-art presentation and RPG Maker origins give it a deliberately modest appearance, yet the unsettling environments demonstrate considerable creativity. Darkness, unusual architectural arrangements, surreal imagery, and unexpected encounters create a persistent sense of unease. The contrast between the protagonist's harmless appearance and the disturbing subject matter strengthens the psychological impact. Rather than depending entirely on conventional jump scares, the game frequently encourages players to anticipate danger through uncertainty and environmental storytelling.

The audiovisual presentation further enhances this uncomfortable atmosphere. Original music establishes an appropriately mysterious tone, while distinctive artwork reinforces the dreamlike nature of the environments. Voice performances contribute personality to important encounters, particularly those involving the eccentric game show host. These elements work together to make the experience feel more elaborate than its relatively simple technical foundation might suggest. Although the visuals lack modern sophistication, their unconventional artistic direction remains effective in communicating the game's unsettling identity.

Replayability represents another significant advantage. Multiple endings, including an additional ninth conclusion introduced through an update, encourage players to revisit the adventure and investigate alternative outcomes. Hidden secrets and branching discoveries provide additional motivation to examine environments carefully. Different conclusions can also influence how players interpret the protagonist's circumstances, making repeated playthroughs worthwhile for those interested in uncovering the larger mystery. Steam achievements and trading cards offer further incentives, while Steam Cloud support adds convenience.

Despite these strengths, the game has several noticeable limitations. Its abstract storytelling sometimes sacrifices clarity, leaving important developments open to interpretation. Certain puzzles and environmental obstacles may also become frustrating when solutions are insufficiently communicated. Players accustomed to clearly defined objectives, extensive character progression, or action-oriented survival horror might find the experience mechanically restrictive. Furthermore, the deliberately obscure narrative may feel unsatisfying to those expecting comprehensive explanations or definitive resolutions.

The mature content is another important consideration. The adventure explores murder, execution, psychological distress, and disturbing personal relationships. Some written material contains unwanted sexually charged remarks and descriptions of violence, while certain endings feature sudden graphic illustrations. Although these elements support the darker themes, they may be uncomfortable for sensitive players. The game's innocent-looking protagonist should therefore not be mistaken for an indication of family-friendly content.

As a free experience, Close Your Eyes [Old Version] offers considerable value. Its unusual storytelling, atmospheric presentation, hidden discoveries, and alternative endings provide an appealing package without requiring an initial purchase. The existence of a substantially reimagined commercial remake does not eliminate the appeal of this earlier interpretation, which retains its own creative identity. Its Very Positive Steam user reception also suggests that its distinctive approach has resonated with many players, particularly those who appreciate unconventional independent horror.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, the game currently carries an Unknown classification rather than an official Verified or Playable designation. Its lightweight system requirements suggest that hardware performance should not be particularly demanding, but compatibility with SteamOS remains unconfirmed. The game officially supports Windows and offers partial controller support, meaning Steam Deck users may need Proton compatibility settings or customized control mappings. Consequently, handheld functionality should be considered uncertain until independently tested.

Ultimately, Close Your Eyes [Old Version] is a memorable psychological horror adventure that succeeds through creativity, atmosphere, and thematic ambition rather than technical complexity. Its unsettling environments, mysterious characters, philosophical undertones, and numerous secrets create a compelling experience for players who enjoy interpreting fragmented narratives. While occasional puzzle frustrations, ambiguous storytelling, and dated mechanics prevent it from achieving universal appeal, its distinctive personality and accessible price make it easy to recommend to enthusiasts of experimental horror.

An imaginative and disturbing indie horror experience featuring memorable psychological storytelling, atmospheric exploration, and rewarding replayability. Its unconventional presentation and narrative ambiguity may not appeal to everyone, but its creativity makes it a worthwhile adventure.

Rating: 8/10
